AS THE AIRCRAFT WAS PASSING THROUGH 24,000 FEET, I NOTICED THE OIL PRESSURE ON THE RIGHT ENGINE WAS STARTING TO DECREASE AT A NOTICEABLE RATE. I INFORMED FT WORTH CENTER OF THE SITUATION AND SAID I NEEDED TO LAND AT THE CLOSEST AIRPORT. THAT AIRPORT BEING KCRT. I INITIATED AN EMERGENCY DESCENT AND WHEN ON A 6 MILE FINAL TO THE AIRPORT THE RED WARNING LIGHT FOR OIL PRESSURE ILLUMINATED. I PULLED THE RIGHT ENGINE THROTTLE TO IDLE AND NOTICED THE OIL PRESSURE RISE AND THE WARNING LIGHT EXTINGUISH. I ELECTED TO LEAVE THE ENGINE RUNNING AT THIS TIME. ON SHORT FINAL THE WARNING LIGHT REILLUMINATED. ONCE I WAS ON THE RUNWAY I SHUTDOWN THE RIGHT ENGINE AND TAXIED INTO THE RAMP AREA. UPON EXITING THE AIRCRAFT I CHECKED THE OIL LEVEL AND THE DIPSTICK SHOWED NO OIL. I WAITED 30 MINUTES FOR THE ENGINE TO COOL AND CHECKED THE OIL LEVEL AGAIN AND STILL NO OIL WAS EVIDENT ON THE DIPSTICK. THE AIRCRAFT ENGINES HAD BEEN SERVICED THE PREVIOUS WEEK BY STEVENS AEROSPACE. I CALLED THEM TO INFORM THEM OF THE SITUATION AND THEY SENT A MOBILE AOG UNIT THAT AFTERNOON. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE MAGNETIC SEAL THAT WAS REPLACED THE PREVIOUS WEEK WAS DEFECTIVE. AFTER CONSULTING WITH THE ENGINE MANUFACTURER IT WAS DECIDED THAT THE BEST COURSE OF ACTION WAS TO REPLACE THE GEARBOX WITH A NEW STYLE, WHICH WOULD ELIMINATE THE NEED FOR THE SEALS. THE ENGINE WAS TEST RUN AND RETURNED TO SERVICE AFTER THE GEAR BOX WAS REPLACED.

INITIATED A LEFT HAND TURN BACK TO BASE, SLOWED AIRSPEED TO APPROXIMATELY 100KIAS, AND ENGAGED NAV/ALT WHILE MEDIC CALLED MED BASE AND INFORMED THEM OF SITUATION. WHEN ESTABLISHED IN STABLE FLIGHT REGIME HEADING BACK TO BASE, HANDED MEDIC THE CHECKLIST AND ASKED HIM TO FIND FADEC FAILURE TO CONFIRM EP BEFORE MOVING ANY TWIST GRIPS. MYSELF AND MEDIC READ/TALKED THROUGH EMERGENCY PROCEDURE. CONFIRMED #2 FADEC FAILURE BY VERIFYING #2 CAUTION SEGMENTS AND COLLECTIVE CHANGES/NEEDLE MOVEMENT. IDENTIFIED #2 TWIST GRIP, PRESSED IDLE STOP RELEASE, AND DECREASED TWIST GRIP TO SET #2 ENGINE N1 TO 80%. CONTINUED FLIGHT TO I18 AND BRIEFED CREW THAT WE WILL BE MAINTAINING SINGLE ENGINE AIRSPEED AND SHOOTING THE APPROACH TO RNWY 22 IN A SINGLE ENGINE/RUN ON LANDING PROFILE, IN CASE #2 ENGINE DETERIORATED. EXECUTED APPROACH AND AS DECELERATING TO A HOVER THE FLI NEEDLES SPLIT AND GOT A LIMIT LIGHT AND AUDIBLE “GONG”. #1 NEEDLE HAD EXCEEDED 12 FLI, BUT DID NOT SEE IT ABOVE 20 SECOND LIMIT “DOT”. REMAINED IN THIS RANGE FOR APPROXIMATELY 2 SECONDS. REDUCED COLLECTIVE AND POWER STABILIZED IN 2.5 MINUTE OEI RANGE AND LIMIT LIGHT EXTINGUISHED. HOVERING WITH A RIGHT CROSSWIND, APPLIED LEFT PEDAL TO TURN AND GOT LIMIT/”GONG” BELOW “DOT” FOR APPROXIMATELY 1 SECOND. DECIDED TO HOVER TO PARKING IN OEI, WAS ABLE TO ALTERNATE BELOW OEI MAX CONTINUOUS AND INTO 2.5 MINUTE OEI LIMIT, SO DID NOT MAKE ANY #2 ENGINE TWIST GRIP ADJUSTMENTS. I KNEW I WAS UNDER OEI OPERATION LIMITS BECAUSE HAD 24% TORQUE INDICATED ON #2 ENGINE, NO LIMIT LIGHT OR “GONG” WHEN OPERATING OVER AEO MAXIMUM TAKE OFF POWER, AND HAD 2.5 MINUTE COUNT DOWN PRESENT WHEN OVER OEI CONTINUOUS POWER LIMIT. HOVERED INTO PARKING AND HAD 1 MINUTE 9 SECONDS LEFT IN OEI RANGE WHEN STARTED LANDING ON DOLLY. COMPLETED LANDING APPROXIMATELY 10 SECONDS LATER. RETARDED #2 TWIST GRIP TO IDLE AS LOWERING COLLECTIVE THEN COMPLETED ACFT SHUTDOWN.

AIRCRAFT DEPARTED KSHR AT 1840Z FOR A MAINTENANCE FLIGHT. DURING CLIMB OUT THE PILOT ASKED THE COPILOT TO MOVE THE TEMPERATURE CONTROL HANDLE FOR HEAT. THE COPILOT OPENED THE HEAT VALVE WITH THE TEMPERATURE CONTROL HANDLE AND EXPERIENCED A SLIGHT "POP". THE HEAT REMAINED IN THE OPEN POSITION FOR A BRIEF TIME UNTIL THE CREW HAD SMOKE IN THE CABIN AND COCKPIT. THE COPILOT ATTEMPTED TO SECURE THE TEMPERATURE CONTROL HANDLE, BUT COULD NOT RETURN THE HANDLE TO THE OFF POSITION DUE TO BINDING. THE CREW IMMEDIATELY RETURNED TO KSH WHERE THE AIRCRAFT WAS INSPECTED FOR THE CAUSE OF THE BINDING AND SMOKE. DURING THE INVESTIGATION IT WAS NOTED THE RIGHT ENGINE BLEED VALVE LINKAGE WAS SLIGHTLY MISADJUSTED CAUSING THE VALVE LEVER AND LINKAGE TO BIND IN AN OVER-CENTER POSITION RESULTING IN THE BLEED VALVES STAYING OPEN. THIS RESULTED IN DAMAGE TO THE INTERIOR INSULATION BLANKETS INSTALLED NEXT TO THE HEATING DUCT AND THIS IS BELIEVED TO BE THE SOURCE OF THE SMOKE. THE LINKAGE WAS ADJUSTED AND AIRCRAFT HEATING SYSTEM WAS OPERATED DURING A GROUND RUN WITH NO FURTHER ADVERSE EFFECTS.

DETECTED BASED ON A CUSTOMER REQUEST REGARDING TEST DATA, THAT MTU-H INCORRECTLY DETERMINED THE N1 MODIFIER LEVEL IN CERTAIN CASES FOR BOEING FADEC ENGINES. FOR POST-SB 73-0288 ECU SOFTWARE THE ESM 72-00-00 TESTING 007 EFFECT C SUBTASK 72-00-00-760-379 REQUIRES TO IDENTIFY THE MODIFIER LEVEL FOR TAKEOFF THRUST MARGIN AND FOR MAXIMUM CONTINUOUS THRUST MARGIN. THE LOWER THRUST MARGIN HAS TO BE USED FOR DETERMINING THE N1 MODIFIER LEVEL. THIS REQUIREMENT HAS NOT BEEN CONSIDERED SUFFICIENTLY BY MTU-H IN THE TESTCELL WORKING DOCUMENTATION AND THEREFORE WAS NOT FOLLOWED DURING TEST. MTU-H IDENTIFIED THE MODIFIER LEVEL USING ONLY THE TAKE-OFF THRUST MARGIN AS IT IS REQUIRED PER ESM 72-00-00 TESTING 007 EFFECT C SUBTASK 72-00-00-760-366 FOR PRE-SB 73-0288 SOFTWARE. MTU-H HAS PERFORMED A TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT WHETHER THERE MIGHT BE A POTENTIAL IMPACT ON OPERATION. THE N1 MODIFIER FUNCTION IS ACTIVATED ONLY IF ALL OF THE FOLLOWING PREREQUISITES ARE FULFILLED: - ECU IN NORM MODE. N1 RPM BETWEEN 96,3% AND 117% - ALTITUDE BELOW13.000 FT- TAKE OFF FLAG LATCHED, MEANING AL THROTTLES => 48 TLA AND PARK BREAK RE-LEASED (THE TAKE OFF FLAG WILL BE AUTOMATICALLY UNLATCHED AFTER 5 MINUTES). MTU-H HAS CONTACTED THE OEM TO CLARIFY THE EM REQUIREMENT AND TO OBTAIN THE OEM FEEDBACK ESPECIALLY IN REGARDS TO FLIGHT SAFETY AND EFFECT ON OPERATION. THE OEM ANSWERED “SOME OPERATORS MAY NOT BE AWARE THAT EGT MARGIN CAN BE GREATER AT TAKEOFF POWER THAN AT THE MXCN SETTING FOR SOME CF6-80C2 INSTALLATIONS. IN SUCH CASES, EGT MARGIN AT MXCN WILL BE DEPLETED BEFORE TAKEOFF MARGIN IS DEPLETED.” (CASE #[NO]). MTU RECALCULATED EGT MARGIN AND N2 MARGIN WITH THE CORRECT MODIFIER FOR ALL AFFECT-ED ENGINES. BOTH MARGINS WERE FOUND WITHIN THE EM LIMIT. THEREFORE, MTU CONCLUDES THAT THERE IS NO EFFECT ON OPERATION AND/OR FLIGHT SAFETY ON THE AFFECTED ENGINES WHEN USING THE N1 MODIFIER LEVEL DETERMINED WITH THE TAKEOFF THRUST MARGIN ONLY. AFFECTED CUSTOMERS ARE INFORMED ABOUT THIS ISSUE.

FROM KSAT TO MYNN WHEN WE EXPERIENCED AN ENGINE FAILURE IN FLIGHT. AT FLIGHT LEVEL 390 APPROXIMATELY 100 MILES WEST OF THE SOUTHERN COAST OF FLORIDA, THE LEFT (#1) ENGINE ROLLED BACK QUITE ABRUPTLY IN FLIGHT. WE DECLARED AN EMERGENCY DUE TO THE LOSS OF THRUST AND THE CABIN PRESSURE RISING SINCE ONLY 1 ENGINE WAS SUPPLYING PRESSURIZATION. UPON OUR DECENT DOWN TO 10,000 FEET, WE COMMENCED OUR SOPS AND RUN THROUGH OUR EMERGENCY CHECKLIST. THE FIRST ONE CALLS TO SECURE THE ENGINE AND TAKE IT OFFLINE. AFTER COMPLETING THIS WE ARE TO MAKE THE DECISION TO TRY AND RESTART IT. BECAUSE THERE WAS NO INDICATION OF FIRE, FOREIGN OBJECT DEBRIS, OR FROZEN FAN (N1 OR N2), WE DECIDED TO RESTART THE ENGINE. AFTER RUNNING THROUGH THE PROPER CHECKLIST TO RESTART THE ENGINE, WE COULD NOT GET THE ENGINE TO LIGHT OFF. SO, WE DECIDED TO RESECURE THE ENGINE AND CONTINUE TO ON TO OUR DIVERSION AIRPORT, KRSW, WITH ONE ENGINE AND LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. WE CONTINUED WITH THE "SINGLE ENGINE APPROACH TO LANDING" CHECKLIST AND LANDED THE PLANE AT KRSW. THIS IS A 12,000FT RUNWAY AND AFTER RUNNING THE LANDING DISTANCE WITH PARTIAL FLAPS WE CONCLUDED IT WAS MORE THAN LONG ENOUGH. THE LANDING ITSELF TURNED OUT TO BE A NON-EVENT AND WE WERE ABLE TO SAFELY TAXI TO THE FBO AND SAFELY DE-PLANE THE PASSENGERS.

FLIGHT CREW REPORTED THAT THE RIGHT ENGINE SHUTDOWN DURING THEIR TAKEOFF ROLL. CREW ABORTED THEIR TAKEOFF AND TAXIED THE AIRCRAFT BACK TO A LOCATION TO FURTHER EVALUATE THE RIGHT ENGINE'S CONDITION. CREW CONTACTED JET OUT'S MAINTENANCE DEPARTMENT, IT WAS THEN DETERMINED TO RESTART THE ENGINE. CREW RAN THE ENGINE WHILE IN CONTACT WITH THE MAINTENANCE DEPARTMENT. AFTER COMPLETION OF THE GROUND RUNS/CHECKS IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE ENGINE/AIRCRAFT WAS OKAY FOR THE FLIGHT TO HOME BASE. DOWNLOADS FROM THE ONBOARD MONITORING SYSTEM (ARES) WERE SENT TO TEXTRON AVIATION FOR REVIEW. THE DOWNLOADS SHOWED THE FLIGHT CREW HAD DEPRESSED THE SWITCH STARTING THE ENGINE, AND DURING THE TAKEOFF ROLL THIS SWITCH APPEARED TO DISENGAGED. DURING FURTHER INVESTIGATION WITH WILLIAMS INTERNATIONAL (ENGINE MANUFACTURE) AND TEXTRON AVIATION (AIRCRAFT MANUFACTURE) WE WERE INFORMED THAT TEXTRON AVIATION IS AWARE OF THE ISSUE. THEY STATED IF THE FLIGHT CREW DOES NOT FULLY DEPRESS THE "RUN/STOP" SWITCH WHEN STARTING THE ENGINE, THE ENGINE WILL START BUT AT SOME POINT DURING AIRCRAFT OPERATION THE SWITCH MAY DISENGAGE, CAUSING THE ASSOCIATED ENGINE TO SHUT DOWN. ALSO, THEY NOTED THAT THE SWITCH MY HANG UP WHEN DEPRESSED, AT THEN DISENGAGE AT A LATER TIME DUE TO VIBRATION FOR EXAMPLE. JET OUT LLC HAS ADDED ADDITIONAL TRAINING TO OUR FLIGHT CREWS TO ADDRESS THIS SITUATION.

LOCAL MAINTENANCE WAS CALLED OUT TO LOOK INTO THE ISSUE, THEY PROCEEDED TO INSPECT THE ENTIRE AIRCRAFT FROM NOSE TO TAIL TRYING TO IDENTIFY ANY CAUSE OF SMOKE/OIL SMELL. MAINTENANCE THEN CHECKED THE ENGINE OIL LEVEL - THE RH ENGINE WAS APPROXIMATELY 3/4 OF A QUART OVER FILLED. THIS HAS BEEN FOUND TO CAUSE OIL TO GET PUSHED INTO THE COMPRESSOR SECTION OF THE ENGINE AND CREATE LIGHT TO HEAVY SMOKE AND THE OIL SMELL THROUGHOUT THE AIRCRAFT INTERIOR. THE OIL QUANTITY WAS ADJUSTED AND HIGH POWER ENGINE RUNS WERE COMPLETED AND ALL SYSTEMS TESTED. NO ISSUES WERE REPORTED. THE AIRCRAFT THEN DEPARTED KDAB FOR INTENDED REPO FLIGHT TO KSAT. AT THIS POINT, I VERY CAUTIOUSLY LOCATED MY ENGINE 2 THROTTLE AND PROCEEDED TO SLOWLY ROLL IT OFF TO SECURE IT. WHILE DOING THIS I REMAINED FOCUSED ON THE NUMBER 1 ENGINE TO MAKE SURE I WAS SECURING THE CORRECT ENGINE. COULD HEAR ATC ATTEMPT TO CONTACT ME ASKING ME TO IDENT WHICH I TRIED AND COULD NOT ACCOMPLISH DUE TO THERE BEING NO POWER TO TRANSPONDER. I COULD HEAR ATC CLEAR US FOR ANY AND ALL RUNWAYS. AS I CONTINUED WITH THE SHALLOW SINGLE ENGINE APPROACH (STILL 1.5 MINUTES OUT) I ACTIVATED THE NR 2 ENGINE EMERGENCY CUTOFF, WHICH ENUNCIATED ACTIVE. MTU WORKING DOCUMENTATION WAS SUBSEQUENTLY REVIEWED AND DID NOT REFLECT APPLICATION OF POLYSULFIDE IN THIS AREA. MTU REVIEWED THE TECHNICAL DATA TO IDENTIFY, WHY THE MATERIAL WAS USED IN THIS AREA. IT WAS SUSPECTED, THAT THE UNKNOWN POLYSULFIDE APPLICATION WAS RELATED TO A DIFFERENT INTERPRETATION OF EM CHAPTER 72-00-24 REPAIR 003 (REPLACEMENT OF DAMAGED SEALS AND REPAIR OF AXIAL AND CIRCUMFERENTIAL CLOSEOUTS) AND 7 2-24-01 REPAIR 013 (TRENCH FILLER AND CLOSEOUT REPAIR). TO VERIFY THIS SUSPICION AND IDENTIFY THE CORRECT PROCEDURE MTU CONTACTED THE OEM AND OPENED CASE NO. #[NO] AND #[NO]. THE OEM STATED, THAT THE USE OF POLYSULFIDE IN THIS AREA IS CORRECT FOR BOTH REPAIRS 003 AND 013 AS BOTH REPAIRS REQUIRE THE APPLICATION OF POLYSULFIDE TO THE SAME CLOSEOUT AREAS. BASED ON THIS INFORMATION MTU INVESTIGATED ON THE WORK ORDERS ALREADY PERFORMED AND IDENTIFIED, THAT ON THE PARTS LISTED IN ATTACHMENT 1 MTU DID NOT APPLY POLYSULFIDE IN THE CLOSEOUT AREA BELOW THE ABRADABLE AS REQUESTED PER EM 72-00-24 REPAIR 003 AND 72-24-01 REPAIR 013. FOLLOWING STEPS OF 72-00-24 REPAIR 003 AND 72-24-01 REPAIR 013 HAVE NOT BEEN PERFORMED: - REPLACEMENT OF THE FIBERGLASS AT THE CLOSE OUTS WITH POLYSULFIDE UNDER THE ABRADABLE INADVERTENTLY NOT PERFORMED, REFER TO SUBTASK 72-00-24-300-004 AND 72-24-01-350-129 - REPLACEMENT OF THE FIBERGLASS AT THE CLOSE OUTS WITH POLYSULFIDE IN THE VERTICAL PART UP TO THE FAN CASE INADVERTENTLY NOT PERFORMED, REFER TO SUBTASK 72-24-01-350-117 AND SUBTASK 72-00-24-300-004 FROM OUR INTERNAL RISK ASSESSMENT, MTU CONSIDERS THE MENTIONED MISSING STEPS AS NOT FLIGHT SAFETY RELEVANT, REQUIRING NO IMMEDIATE ACTIONS. THE RISK, THAT WAS IDENTIFIED, IS PRIMARILY, THAT THE MOISTURE CAN GET THROUGH THE GAP BETWEEN TWO ADJACENT TRENCH FILLERS, AND THE MOISTURE MIGHT LEAD TO CORROSION. THIS CORROSION CAN POTENTIALLY LEAD TO UN-SERVICEABILITY OF THE PART AT THE NEXT SHOP INSPECTION, BUT NO ULTIMATE FAILURE OF THE PART, WHICH WOULD LEAD TO A SAFETY RELEVANT EVENT. FURTHERMORE, FOR ALL IN SHOP HANDLED FAN STATOR MODULES, NO FINDINGS IN THE FIBERGLASS CLOSEOUTS WERE IDENTIFIED, WHICH WOULD MAKE A REPAIR MANDATORY. THE APPLICATION OF POLYSULFIDE AS PART OF REPAIR 003 AND 013 IS A PROACTIVE MEASURE TO PREVENT FUTURE ENTRY OF MOISTURE IN THE SPLIT LINE. MTU SHOP HANDLING GUIDE WORK SCOPE LEVEL TSO1 REQUIRED REPAIR 003 AS THIS PROACTIVE MEASURE. REPAIR 13 IS REQUIRED BASED ON FINDINGS PER EM INSPECTION. MTU CONTACTED THE OEM FOR TECHNICAL SUPPORT AND TO CONFIRM THE RISK ASSESSMENT AS WELL AS TERMINATING ACTIONS SUGGESTED BY MTU, REFER TO CASE #[NO] OPENED 04. MARCH 2025. DURING ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS THE ISHIKAWA- AND 5-WHY-METHOD WAS USED TO IDENTIFY THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE INCORRECT POLYSULFIDE APPLICATION. WITHIN THE FRAMEWORK OF ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS THE FOLLOWING CONTRIBUTING FACTORS WERE IDENTIFIED: THE ERROR OCCURRED DURING THE WORK PLANNING PROCESS WHEN THE WORK PLANNER INTENDED TO TRANSFER THE REQUIREMENTS FROM THE ENGINE MANUAL REPAIR INTO MTU INTERNAL WORKING DOCUMENTATION. WHILE TRANSFERRING THE OEM REPAIR INFORMATION THE WORK PLANNER MISINTERPRETED THE ENGINE MANUAL REQUIREMENTS REGARDING THE NECESSITY OF THE REPLACEMENT OF THE FIBERGLASS WITH POLYSULFIDE AT THE CLOSE OUTS UNDER THE ABRADABLE AND THE VERTICAL PART UP TO THE FAN CASE AS PART OF REPAIR 003 AND REPAIR 013 INCORRECTLY. THE REQUIREMENTS FOR THE REMOVAL OF THE FIBERGLASS IS BASED ON THE PMI AND IS DESCRIBED IN EM 72-00-24 INSPECTION 002 AND WAS THEREFORE MISSED TO BE CONSIDERED WHEN REPAIR 003 WAS PLANNED. ONE ELEMENT OF REPAIR 013 IS THE REPLACEMENT OF THE FIBERGLASS WITH POLYSULFIDE AT THE CLOSE OUTS. IN THE LATER INDUSTRIALIZATION OF EM 72-24-01 REPAIR 013, THE INCLUDED NOTE REGARDING THE DEFINITION OF THE PROCESSING AREA, BASED ON EXISTING EXPERIENCE AND THE COMPLEX NESTING OF MULTIPLE REPAIRS, WAS OVERLOOKED. BOTH PLANNED REPAIRS UNDERWENT A FOUR-EYE CHECK BY QUALIFIED STAFF (INCLUDING VERIFICATION AGAINST THE EM) AND A FIRST ARTICLE REVIEW BY THE RELEVANT PRODUCTION DEPARTMENT AND QUALITY CONTROL, WITHOUT THE ERROR BEING DETECTED. OUR POWER SETTING WERE LIKELY 1.5PSI TO 2PSI BELOW MAX TORQUE, AS THIS IS GENERALLY WHERE I LIKE TO SET THE POWER. OUR ITT’S WERE WELL WITHIN THE NORMAL RANGE (LIKELY AROUND 710) AND OUR NG’S WERE NORMAL ALSO. THESE SPECIFIC NUMBERS CAN BE PULLED. THERE WERE NO INDICATIONS THAT THE SURGES OR STALLS (WHICHEVER THEY WERE) AFFECTED THE ENGINE INDICATIONS, THOUGH I REDUCED POWER QUICKLY AFTER THE EVENT TO GET IT TO STOP. THE SEPARATOR WAS CLOSED IN VMC CONDITIONS. I REDUCED POWER IN HOPING TO FIND A SWEET SPOT WHERE THE BLASTS WERE NOT OCCURRING AND PULLED THE PCL BACK TO HAVE THE NG IN THE SINGLE DIGIT RANGE. THIS HAD THE EFFECT THAT I WAS LOOKING FOR WITH A CESSATION OF THE SURGES AND SPARKS FOR THE MOST PART. ANY POWER INPUTS THEREAFTER ON OUR WAY TO THE NEAREST AIRPORT BROUGHT BACK THE SURGES AND SPARKS. I FELT AS IF I COULD GET AN INCREASE IN POWER FROM THE ENGINE, AND DID SO A FEW TIMES, BUT THE SPARKING AND SURGE/STALLS INCREASED AS WELL. THE SPARKS ALSO CONTINUED INTERMITTENTLY ON THE WAY TO THE AIRPORT, BUT NOT AS MANY AS WHEN EVENT INITIALLY STARTED. AROUND 5 MILES AWAY FROM THE AIRPORT WE DID START TO SMELL SMOKE, BUT NOT THAT WAS VISIBLE NOR SEEMED TO BE WORKING ITS WAY INTO THE COCKPIT TO ANY SIGNIFICANT DEGREE. WE WERE SET UP FOR THE ILS AND VECTORED TO LOSE ALTITUDE. WE BROKE OUT OF AN OVERCAST LAYER WHICH MAY HAVE BEEN 2500 TO 3500’. I CALLED FOR THE GEAR AND FLAPS WHEN WE WERE MAYBE ¼ OF A MILE FROM THE RUNWAY TO ENSURE WE WOULD MAKE IT. I DID NOT USE BETA OR REVERSE AND WE ROLLED OUT NEAR THE FAR END OF THE RUNWAY.

AFTER THE FIRST FAILURE I CONTACTED THE MANUFACTURER WHO SAID THEY HAD NOT SEEN A FAILURE LIKE THAT AND ASKED ME TO SEND THE SPARK TO THEM FOR INSPECTION. THEY SENT A REPLACEMENT BACK. I SPOKE WITH THE MANUFACTURER (POWERMASTER ENGINES), THEY STATED THEY SAW A RASH OF FAILURES LIKE THIS WITH THIS PARTICULAR PLUG A FEW YEARS BACK. MY CONCERN HERE IS THAT THERE IS A BAD BATCH OF PLUGS FLOATING AROUND. WE HAVE LOST 3 PLUGS IN 68 HOURS - TWO OF THEM AT THE SAME TIME IN THE SAME CYLINDER. ON 09/2/25 WE WERE DEPARTING RUNWAY 21 AT KCNM. AT V1 DURING OUR TAKE ROLL WE HEARD A VERY AUDIBLE IMPACT OR “ THUD” AIRCRAFT RIGHT. THE IMPACT INDUCED A SIGNIFICANT RIGHT YAW. THERE WAS ALSO A MOMENTARY EICAS CAUTION MESSAGE. IT CLEARED BEFORE BEING ABLE TO IDENTIFY IT. WE BELIEVE IT WAS “ENGINE TLA NOT IN TAKE OFF”. THIS WAS PROBABLY INDUCED BY MY HANDS BEING PULLED BACK SLIGHTLY DURING THE INITIAL IMPACT OR YAW. CONTINUED THE TAKE OFF AND PROCEEDED THE INITIAL CLIMB SEQUENCE WITH OUT INCIDENT. OUR INITIAL DIAGNOSIS WAS A POSSIBLE BLOWN TIRE. ALL ENGINE INSTRUMENTS WERE NORMAL. WE PROCEEDED TO KMAF FOR SEVERAL FACTORS AFFECTING SAFETY. ONCE IN “CRUISE” WE CONTACTED AIRCRAFT AT CNM AND THE AIRPORT STAFF TO LOOK FOR DEBRIS ON RUNWAY 21. ALL REPORTS WERE NEGATIVE ON DEBRIS. WE BRIEFED THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS AND PASSENGERS FOR A POSSIBLE “ABNORMAL” LANDING. WE COMMUNICATED WITH MAF APPROACH ABOUT OUR CONDITION AND THEY ADVISED THEY WOULD HAVE RESCUE SERVICES ON STAND BY. WE COORDINATED WITH MAF ATC AND CONDUCTED A LOW APPROACH USING 34L RNAV WITH THE GEAR DOWN. THE APPROACH WAS CONDUCTED AND MIDLAND REPORTED THEY DID NOT OBSERVE ANY ABNORMALITIES. WE THEN CONDUCTED A NORMAL LANDING WITHOUT INCIDENT. UPON PARKING AND ENGINE SHUT DOWN WE CONDUCTED AN INSPECTION. WE OBSERVED INDICATIONS OF A BIRD STRIKE ON THE NUMBER 2 ENGINE. THIS WAS FURTHER VALIDATED BY AN EICAS CAUTION MESSAGE “ENG 2 T2 HEAT FAIL”. THESE OBSERVATIONS LED US TO BELIEVE THERE WAS SUFFICIENT INDICATIONS OF A BIRD BEING INGESTED IN THE RIGHT ENGINE. THESE FACTORS WERE DELIVERED TO THE DIRECTOR OF AVIATION AND DIRECTOR OF MAINTENANCE WHO COLLECTIVELY AGREED TO GROUND THE AIRCRAFT PENDING INSPECTION. ENGINE WAS BOROSCOPED WITH NO DISCREPANCIES NOTED.

ON JUNE 12TH, 2025, PHOENIX AIR GROUP, INC. (PAG) WAS TRANSPORTING PASSENGERS FROM POINT MUGU NAVAL AIR STATION (KNTD) TO SAN NICOLAS ISLAND NAVAL OUTLYING FIELD (KNSI) USING AIRCRAFT [TESCIL]. ONCE THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN CLIMBING TO ITS CRUISE ALTITUDE, CAPTAIN 1 (CA1) AND FIRST OFFICER 1 (FO1) NOTICED SIGNS OF A LEFT ENGINE FAILURE AND RESPONDED TO AN ENGINE FAILURE. FLIGHT ATTENDANT 1 (FA1) NOTIFIED CA1 OF THE ENGINE FIRE, AND CA1 ATTEMPTED TO PUT OUT THE ENGINE FIRE WHILE FO1 DECLARED AN EMERGENCY TO AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL (ATC). CA1 SUCCESSFULLY EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE MID-FLIGHT. FIRE TRUCKS WERE ON STANDBY AS THE AIRCRAFT WAS LANDING, THE AIRCRAFT LANDED SAFELY, AND THE FIRE DEPARTMENT CONFIRMED THAT THE FIRE HAD BEEN EXTINGUISHED AND THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS SAFE TO RETURN TO THE TERMINAL TO UNLOAD PASSENGERS. ENGINE 1 SUSTAINED SUBSTANTIAL FIRE DAMAGE, BUT THE FIRE WAS CONTAINED WITHOUT AIRFRAME FIRE OR EXPLOSION. BASED ON EXAMINATION BY PHOENIX AIR GROUP’S MAINTENANCE TECHNICIANS, EVIDENCE INDICATES THAT THE EVENT WAS PRECIPITATED BY A SUDDEN STOPPAGE OF THE CORE COMPONENTS OF THE ENGINE’S ROTATING ASSEMBLY, CONSISTENT WITH A MAIN SHAFT BEARING FAILURE. THIS SUDDEN STOPPAGE DISRUPTED THE ANNULAR COMBUSTION PATTERN WITHIN THE BURNER CAN, PERMITTING UNBURNED FUEL TO MIGRATE INTO THE TAILPIPE, WHERE IT IGNITED. ONCE THE CREW EXECUTED THE ENGINE SHUTDOWN AND FIRE CHECKLIST THE TAILPIPE FIRE EXTINGUISHED.

DURING FLIGHT, PILOT REPORTED FUEL FLOW DISCREPANCY AND ENGINE ROUGHNESS AND RETUNRED TO BASE FOR A PRECAUTIONARY, ALBEIT IF VERY STRESSFUL, LANDING. UPON INSPECTION OF THE FUEL FLOW SENSOR ( PART OF THE JPI 930 ENGINE INSTRUMENTAION - STC SA01435SA ) IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE FLOW METER PINS ( A FLOSCAN 201 UNIT PROVIDED FROM JPI ) HAD BEEN INCORRECTLY TERMINATED. THE MALE PINS HAD BEEN CRIMPED ON WIRES THAT WERE STRIPPED TO LONG. THESE UNITS WERE SHIPPED FROM JPI PINNED AND INSIDE A TERMINAL BLOCK, MAKING VISUAL INSPECTION DIFFICULT WITHOUT PIN REMOVAL. ADDITIONALY, WHO UNPINS ITEMS SHIPPED FROM THE "MANUFACTURER" JUST TO CHECK- WHILE THE PART OF THE PIN THAT WAS SUPPOSED TO BE ON THE BARE WIRE CONDUCTOR WAS CRIMPED CORRECTLY, THE SECOND CRIMP WHICH IS SUPPOSED TO BE ON THE INSULATION ( STRAIN RELIEF ) WAS ALSO CRIMPED ON THE CONDUCTOR, WHICH IS INCORRECT. THE SECOND CRIMP WAS ALSO LOOSE, AS THE THE INSULATION WHICH WOULD NOMALLY BE A PART OF THE OVERALL THICKNESS, WAS ABSCENT. THIS LOOSE CRIMP, AND ABSCENT STRAIN RELIEF , ALLOWED THE WIRES TO FLEX AND EVENTAULLY BREAK. WHILE ONLY ONE OF THE THREE WIRES BROKE, THE OTHERS HAD LESS THAN 25% OF THIER STRANDS INTACT. SUBSEQUENT INSECTIONS OF OTHER AC IN OUR FLEET, WITH SIMILAR FLOSCAN UNITS FROM THE SAME STC, REVEALED 2 OTHER UNITS WITH THE SAME ISSUE. IN TOTAL, WE FOUND 3 FLOSCAN 201 UNITS ( SN'S 218375, 223453, AND 230659 ) ALL WITH THE SAME MISCRIMPED PINS. WE HAD AT LEAST ONE ADDITIONAL UNIT THAT WAS REMOVED PREVIOUSLY "INOP" THAT WE COULDNT VERIFY AS IT WAS DISCARDED.
